clue.text: Pastime I'd ignobly dub "freakish"

indicators.note: freakish suggests something misshapen and abnormal, so the quoted letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a muscle-building hobby is ignoble and freakish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freakish' rearranges the twelve letters of I'D IGNOBLY DUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing one's muscles through weight training is a hobby many people pursue, so it is a pastime.

clue.text: Translation of "Fledermaus" originally sanctioned by Mr Strauss?

parts.note: Fledermaus is the German word for the flying mammal called a bat

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word sanctioned, its first letter

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man

explanation.surface: An English version of the operetta Die Fledermaus approved by its composer, Johann Strauss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Johann Strauss the composer, but the Strauss meant is Andrew Strauss, the England cricket captain and opening bat; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Strauss was an England cricketer who opened the batting, so he is an example of one who bats.

clue.text: After no-ball bouncer Somerset tailender's out of action for a while

definitions.text: out of action for a while

indicators.note: After places the Somerset piece behind the shortened bouncer
no in front of ball tells us one ball-shaped letter is taken away from the bouncer

parts.note: a bouncer is a doorman at a club
a ball is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: a tailender bats last, so this asks for the final letter of Somerset

explanation.surface: A cricket report: after a no-ball bouncer, Somerset's tailender is injured and out for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes an O out of the bouncer and 'After' puts T behind what is left. The cricket terms are misdirection: a bouncer is a short fast ball, a tailender a weak lower-order batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive for the time being, like a sleeping volcano, temporarily out of action.

clue.text: Complain as femme fatale entertains docked pleasure boat

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside one's home, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful, alluring woman

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is docked, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a yacht is a boat sailed for pleasure

explanation.surface: A seductive woman hosts guests on a luxury boat tied up in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' drops the boat's last letter, and 'entertains' puts the rest inside the belle. Docked suggests a boat in port, but here it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is informal slang for grumbling or moaning, so it means to complain.

clue.text: Finally altogether assimilated

indicators.note: what is assimilated is absorbed within something, so the answer sits inside the word Finally

explanation.surface: At last everything has been absorbed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total or all told, which is what altogether means when counting up.

clue.text: Opening debate on US visionary

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from debate

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
Amer. is an abbreviation for American, i.e. US

explanation.surface: A speaker opens a debate on America with a sweeping vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is someone with idealistic, imaginative ideas, a person who dreams of what might be.

clue.text: Miser drawing a grand less in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
less means minus, taking the grand's letter away

parts.note: drawing a cart is dragging it along
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted pensioner draws his pension a thousand short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes a G from DRAGGING to leave DRAGGIN; 'in retirement' turns that round. The 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is an old word for a stingy person who hoards money, the same as a miser.

clue.text: A gym complies with arrangement for sporting event

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A gym meets the rules for hosting a big sports competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with arrangement' rearranges the letters of A GYM COMPLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern Olympics are the world's largest multi-sport competition held every four years.

clue.text: After a bit of loving on the side

parts.note: later means afterwards

indicators.note: a bit of the word loving is its first letter

explanation.surface: Following some affection, an illicit affair on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, as in a lateral movement sideways.

clue.text: Maintain exterior to English classic car

indicators.note: being exterior to something means wrapping around its outside

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert something

explanation.surface: Someone insists on the outside of an old English car being kept up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hillman Avenger was a British family saloon of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hillman Avenger was a 1970s British saloon now regarded as a vintage model.

clue.text: Blur rejoin roadie somewhere in South America

indicators.note: to blur something is to smear it out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The band Blur takes back a roadie for a tour of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British rock band, which suggests the roadie; here it rearranges REJOIN ROADIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian city, a place located in South America.

clue.text: Dam next to railway in Bristol?

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, and mamma is mother

explanation.surface: A dam beside a railway line in the city of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristols' is British rhyming slang for breasts (Bristol City = titty), so the question mark marks something found in a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammary means relating to the breasts, which rhyming slang calls Bristols, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Not the first vertical back to get back pain

indicators.note: not the first means without its opening letter

parts.note: plumb means exactly vertical, as with a plumb line
ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: Standing upright again brings back the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' drops P from PLUMB to give LUMB. The first 'back' means AGO; the second is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles and joints of the lower spine.

clue.text: Roughly speaking, isn't tinnitus ringing?

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, as a ring encircles, so tinnitus holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: Isn't tinnitus just a sort of ringing in the ears?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like the ear complaint's symptom, but it means encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is a slangy, casual contraction of isn't it, used in rough colloquial speech.

clue.text: University town, original of Candleford, imaginary home to the Bull

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in the radio soap The Archers, home to the Bull pub

explanation.surface: Literary towns: Lark Rise to Candleford and a fictional village with a pub called the Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in the fictional village of Ambridge, whose pub is the Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English town famous for its ancient university.

clue.text: Male key worker hiding bungle

indicators.note: hiding something means concealing it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys; isle is island
a hand is a worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: A man who holds the keys is covering up a botched job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts the worker inside the island. Key means a small low island here, not something that opens a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle a task is to manage it badly, i.e. to botch or bungle it.

clue.text: They are ill-defined signs of ageing

definitions.meaning: matters with no clear boundary between right and wrong
patches of hair turning colour with age

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unclear zones between categories, and literally patches where hair has lost colour with age.

clue.text: Impose ban on Robert Mugabe, actively ostracising capricious brute

indicators.note: actively here means in a lively, rearranged way, so the letters of Robert Mugabe are mixed
ostracising means shutting out, so the letters of brute are removed
capricious means unpredictable, so the brute's letters may come in any order

explanation.surface: Sanctions are imposed on Zimbabwe's leader, excluding an unpredictable tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ROBERT MUGABE, remove those of BRUTE in any order, and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade, so to embargo is to impose a ban.

clue.text: Paying close attention as debts change hands

indicators.note: the right letters are swapped for left ones, R for L, as hands change

parts.note: arrears are debts overdue

explanation.surface: Debts transferred to another owner while someone listens carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) and L (left) are standard abbreviations; 'change hands' turns the first two Rs of ARREARS into Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all ears is an idiom for listening eagerly and attentively.

clue.text: A Greek star

definitions.meaning: the Greek letter corresponding to A
the brightest star in a constellation

explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter, and the label for a constellation's brightest star.

clue.text: Not in favour of touching

definitions.meaning: in contact with, as leaning on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: The word means opposed to something, and also in physical contact, as in leaning one thing on another.

clue.text: Wages squeeze is beginning to lacerate east Scottish town

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to hold it tight within, so pay goes round the rest

parts.note: wages are pay

indicators.note: the beginning of lacerate is its first letter

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A pay freeze begins to hurt a town in Scotland's east.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley is a large town just west of Glasgow; 'east' is a piece, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is a large town in Renfrewshire in western Scotland.

clue.text: US port's wind-powered structures

definitions.meaning: belonging to Mobile, a port city in Alabama
hanging decorations moved by air currents

explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is an Alabama port, and mobiles are hanging sculptures that turn in moving air.

clue.text: Wild West's brothels

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of West's are scrambled

explanation.surface: The bordellos of the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S here counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews is an archaic word for houses of ill repute, i.e. brothels.

clue.text: A pair of aristocrats wallowing in immorality and sin

indicators.note: something wallowing in mud is surrounded by it, so vice wraps round the pair

parts.note: vice is immorality

indicators.note: a pair of letters from the start of aristocrats, its first two

explanation.surface: Two nobles indulge themselves in decadence and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pair of' takes AR, the first two letters of aristocrats; the opening A also stands for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, or greed, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Jagged edges of scythe are, we hear, doubly corroded

indicators.note: the edges of scythe are its first and last letters
doubly means the sound-letter appears twice
we hear marks a word as spoken, the letter R sounding like it

parts.note: said aloud, the word are sounds like the letter R
ate, as acid ate the metal, means corroded

explanation.surface: The blade of a scythe is said to be badly rusted and rough-edged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Serrate means having a notched, saw-toothed edge, like a bread knife.

clue.text: Top deep-sea fisherman, one who uses bait

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, taken from deep-sea

parts.note: an angler is a fisherman with rod and line

explanation.surface: A leading deep-sea fisherman relies on bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who uses bait' reads as fishing, but a dangler dangles a lure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dangles something tempting in front of others offers bait, as a lure.

clue.text: "What's inside is outside", relative will say, conclusively and without self-contradiction

indicators.note: is outside means it goes round the relative

parts.note: content is what is contained inside something
sis is short for sister, a relative

indicators.note: conclusively points to the closing letters of will and say

explanation.surface: A relative states paradoxically that the inside is the outside, yet claims to be logical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusively' gives L and Y, the last letters of 'will say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting consistently means always in the same coherent way, never contradicting oneself.
